purpose: Diagnose whether scalar approximate-state quality metrics are sufficient for finite-time two-term PF cost calibration.

source.direct_truth_policy: Reuse H01 exact-ground direct costs and branch audit; add no direct PF eigenvalue calculations.

controlled_state_construction.definition: sqrt(1-q)|psi0> + exp(i phi)sqrt(q)|chi>, q=target_energy_error/(<chi|H|chi>-E0), with chi the normalized component of the named approximate state orthogonal to psi0

evaluation.direct_pf_reference: H01 exact-ground direct grid minimum cost
evaluation.constructive_counterexample: A phase quartet with invariant energy error, variance, residual norm, and exact overlap that changes PF choice or exceeds either meaningful spread threshold.
primary_outputs: two-term coefficient error relative to exact-state echo
phase-quartet scalar invariance and response spread
descriptive correlations of scalar diagnostics with calibration error

scope_limits: Development-only oracle diagnostic, not an independent holdout.
Exact ground state is used to construct controlled states and only to diagnose mechanism.
No new direct PF eigenvalue points are computed.
No PF coefficients, model powers, thresholds, molecules, bases, or target precision are changed.
This does not establish an operational cheap calibration method.
